summary.one_liner: A 2012 Google Research blog interview in which Senior Staff Software Engineer Ben Appleton describes moving from the Maps team to Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) and working on the Blobstore storage service.
use_cases: Understanding what an SRE role involves compared with a software engineering role
Researching career moves from feature development to production infrastructure
Learning how Google structures SRE on-call and coding time
Reading about large-scale storage design goals such as availability and durability
summary.what_it_does: The page is a Q&A interview posted in July 2012 on the Google Research blog. Ben Appleton describes his path from a Ph.D. in image segmentation to a Software Engineer role on the Maps team in Sydney, and then to SRE. He compares the two roles, saying SRE work is closer to production and focused on large scale, with on-call one week in six versus one week in three on Maps. He reports his coding time rising from 50% to 80%. He also describes his work on Blobstore, a storage service built on Bigtable, and the reliability and efficiency demands it faces. The post ends with advice on applying for SRE roles, including the "Software Engineer, Google.com" and "Systems Engineer, Google.com" job titles.
notable: First-hand account of a developer moving into SRE, with on-call and coding-time comparisons
Describes Blobstore, a Bigtable-based storage service for user binary data
Explains Google's 'Google.com' job title convention for production roles versus R&D
caveats: Dated 2012 and describes Google's internal practices at that time, which may no longer apply
Is an interview with one engineer, so it reflects personal experience rather than official SRE policy
